request.goal:
Build a dependency-free Node.js 24 warehouse stock reconciliation CLI from two CSV inputs. No web server or browser UI.

Entry point: node stock-reconcile.js --opening <path> --events <path> --out <directory>. --help documents usage and exits 0. Successful reconciliation exits 0 and writes stock.csv and audit.json into the output directory. Errors exit nonzero, identify input/row on stderr, and preserve existing outputs and inputs byte-for-byte; wording is otherwise unspecified. Refuse output destinations that would overwrite either input. Validate the entire dataset before publishing outputs. No network calls or npm runtime dependencies.

CSV: UTF-8 with optional BOM, LF/CRLF, quoted commas, doubled quotes and embedded newlines. Require exact headers below; reject malformed quoting, missing/extra columns and blank IDs. Final newline allowed; internal blank records refused. IDs are case-sensitive; do not trim. Quantities must consist of decimal digits and be safe integers; opening onHand may be zero, event quantities must be positive. Reject arithmetic beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER rather than silently rounding.

opening.csv header: sku,onHand. Each SKU occurs exactly once. Initial reserved quantity is zero. events.csv header: id,sku,type,quantity,ref. Apply rows in file order. All SKUs must exist in opening.csv. Supported types:
- RECEIVE: ref must be empty; add quantity to onHand.
- RESERVE: ref is a new, nonempty reservation ID, globally unique within this reconciliation; reserve quantity only when onHand minus reserved is sufficient. onHand is unchanged.
- RELEASE: ref names an existing reservation on the same SKU; release up to its remaining reserved quantity. onHand is unchanged. A fully released reservation cannot be reused under the same ID.
- SHIP: ref names an existing reservation on the same SKU; ship up to its remaining quantity, subtracting the quantity from onHand and reserved.
- RETURN: ref names an earlier SHIP event ID on the same SKU; add quantity back to onHand, without recreating a reservation. Cumulative returns for a shipment cannot exceed that shipment's quantity.
All quantities and balances must stay nonnegative. Unknown references, cross-SKU references, over-release, over-shipment and over-return are errors. Event IDs are global: repeating an identical parsed row with the same ID is an idempotent duplicate and has no effect; the same ID with different fields is an error. Check duplicates before transitions; a repeated shipment after reservation exhaustion stays harmless.

stock.csv has header sku,onHand,reserved,available and rows sorted by SKU using JavaScript string comparison, with correct CSV escaping and LF line endings. Include zero-stock SKUs. audit.json is deterministic, without timestamps/temporary paths; record each event row's ID, applied/duplicate disposition and before/after onHand,reserved,available for its SKU. Also expose counts of applied and duplicate rows. An opening-only reconciliation is valid.

Provide npm test using node:test, with subprocess tests that execute the CLI on isolated temporary directories. Cover successful partial reservation/release/shipment/return sequences, repeated shipment IDs, conflicting duplicates, invalid prerequisites, overflow, quoted multiline identifiers, CRLF/BOM inputs, deterministic repeat execution and preservation of pre-existing outputs on a late invalid row. Assert setup and resulting state, not only exit status.

Provide examples and a README with usage, formats and rules. As a fixed acceptance example: opening A=10 and B=0; RESERVE 6 of A under R1, SHIP 4 under R1 with event ID S1, repeat exactly S1, RELEASE 2 under R1, RETURN 3 referencing S1, RECEIVE 7 of B, RESERVE 2 of B under R2. Final A is onHand=9,reserved=0,available=9; B is onHand=7,reserved=2,available=5; applied rows=6 and duplicate rows=1. A further RETURN 2 referencing S1 must fail and preserve existing outputs. Report executed evidence, actual corrections and gaps accurately.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI runs on Node.js 24 without dependencies or network access; help works and inputs are never overwritten.
CSV parsing handles BOM, CRLF, quoted commas, doubled quotes and newlines; invalid syntax, columns and quantities are refused.
All five event types enforce stock, reservation and return prerequisites, including same-SKU references and safe integer arithmetic.
Identical event IDs are idempotent before transition checks; conflicting duplicates fail without changing existing outputs.
The fixed example yields A=9/0/9, B=7/2/5, six applied rows and one duplicate; excess return fails preserving outputs.
Stock CSV and per-row before/after audit JSON are deterministic; zero-stock SKUs and opening-only input work.
Subprocess regression tests pass, cover late failure preservation and hostile CSV cases, and the report accurately states observed results.

assessment: New CLI use case, not a controlled speed comparison. Inspect executed subprocess tests, state transitions, failure preservation and report against actual observations.
